text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on October 6 in history.
1536 - English religious reformer and bible translator William Tyndale was burned at the stake as a heretic at Vilvarde, near Brussels, on the orders of King Henry VIII.
1552 - Matteo Ricci born. Italian Jesuit Missionary to China where he had much success and spent the last 30 years of his life.
1767 - Henri Christophe born in Grenada. Originally a slave he joined the insurgents against the French in Haiti and went on to be President in 1807. He was named King of Haiti in 1811.
1769 - Sir Isaac Brock born. British soldier and administrator in Canada, popularly known as the "Hero of Canada" during the war of 1812 against the United States.
1773 - Louis Philippe, King of France 1830-1848, born. Known as the "Citizen King".
1808 - Frederick VII born. King of Denmark from 1848-1863. He renounced absolute rule and adopted a representative government.
1820 - Jenny Lind (Johanna Maria Lind) born. Swedish operatic soprano known as the "Swedish Nightingale".
1846 - George Westinghouse born. U.S. engineer and inventor and founder of the Westinghouse Electric Corporation in 1886.
1892 - Alfred, Lord Tennyson, English poet and Poet Laureate from 1850, died.
1902 - The 2,000-mile railway link between Johannesburg and Beira, in Mozambique, was completed.
1903 - Ernest (Thomas Sinton) Walton born. Irish physicist and pioneer of nuclear physics. Co-developed the first nuclear particle accelerator.
1908 - Carole Lombard born as Jane Alice Peters. U.S. film actress and wife of Clark Gable. She was at the height of her popularity when she died in an air crash in 1942.
1914 - Thor Heyerdahl born. Norwegian anthropologist and explorer and leader of several expeditions, notably the "Kon-Tiki".
1927 - The film "The Jazz Singer" starring Al Jolson opened in New York. It was the first full-length feature film to include spoken dialogue and is regarded as the first "talkie".
1928 - Upon the introduction of a new constitution, Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek became President of the Republic of China.
1930 - Hafez al-Assad, president of Syria since independence in 1946, born.

1949 - "Tokyo Rose" (Mrs Iva Toguri D'Aquino), who broadcast Japanese propaganda to U.S. forces in the Pacific during World War Two, was sentenced in San Francisco to 10 years imprisonment and fined $10,000 treason charges.
1970 - Military junta took power in Bolivia following the resignation of President Alfredo Ovando Candia. General Juan Jose Torres declared himself President.
1972 - Over 200 people were killed and over 1,000 injured in a railway disaster in Saltillo, Mexico.
1973 - Egypt and Syria launched attacks on Israeli positions on the East bank of Suez and the Golan Heights, the start of the Yom Kippur war.
1976 - The military seized power in Thailand following violent clashes between police and students.
1978 - Ayatolloh Khomeini, Iranian religious leader opposed to the Shah, was granted asylum in France after being expelled from Iran.
1981 - President Anwar Sadat of Egypt was shot dead by Moslem extremists as he watched a military parade in Cairo.
1989 - U.S. film actress Bette Davis died in Paris.
1991 - Elizabeth Taylor married her eighth husband, builder Larry Fortensky.
